Subject: FinWise pilot — perf/SLO follow-up & next steps

Hi Jack / Alice —

Great call earlier — thanks for walking through FinWise's expected workloads. Quick recap and proposed next steps so we're aligned before the load test:

Summary of perf targets you confirmed on the call:
- Typical 95th latency target (text-gen): < 250 ms
- 99th pct target: <= 400 ms (non-streaming requests)
- Streaming token/chunk latency: < 150 ms from Redwood endpoint to client (token-level streaming sensitivity)
- Throughput: steady-state ~100 reqs/sec, peak bursts up to ~400 reqs/sec for 10-15 minute windows
- Concurrency: sustained 50 concurrent sessions per region; occasional spikes to 200 sessions

Load test coordination (customer-led):
- You said FinWise will run the customer-led k6/Locust scripts against our sandbox/test endpoint. To support that we need:
  - IP allowlist entries (we'll provide our IPs / you provide yours)
  - Test account credentials & scoped API key (we'll issue a short-lived key with elevated quotas for the window)
  - Sample prompt mix / payload sizes so we can mirror token distribution
  - Preferred test windows (we proposed 17 Mar; you suggested later — see below)

Attachments: included a k6 template and a redwood test account stub (redwood_test_account_details.txt) for your team to use as a starting point.

Proposed test window options (UTC):
- Option A: 2027-03-17 01:00-04:00 UTC
- Option B: 2027-03-18 02:00-05:00 UTC (longer monitoring if you want more headroom)

Next steps / asks:
1) Confirm which window you prefer.
2) Share the k6/Locust script you plan to run (we can review and suggest improvements).
3) Provide the source IPs or CIDR ranges you will run the test from so we can pre-populate allowlists.
4) Share representative prompt mix / CSV with token distribution.

Marissa (cc'd) — can you review the k6 template for streaming/keepalive behavior? Aditya, can you scope the temporary quota bump and monitoring for the selected window?

Thanks — looking forward to the test and validating we meet the SLOs.

— Logan

On Mon, Mar 15, 2027 at 9:30 AM Logan Wright <logan.wright@redwood.com> wrote:
> Forwarding Jack's reply and the FinWise script.

Thanks Logan — looked through FinWise's k6. Quick notes / edits inline below and attached is our suggested version (finwise_k6_test_script.js):

- Ramp pattern: use a smoother ramp-up to avoid artificial spikes. Suggested stages: ramp to 100 RPS over 10m, maintain 60m steady-state, then short bursts to 400 RPS for 10-15m.
- Connection reuse: ensure keepalive is enabled on the HTTP client. For streaming tests, use a single persistent connection per VU when possible to validate chunk latency.
- Streaming validation: add assertions that check per-chunk arrival times and emit events when chunk latency > 150ms. k6's default HTTP streaming helpers aren't perfect; we suggest using the custom WS/chunk listener we added in the attached script.
- Metrics: make sure they export p50/p95/p99 for both end-to-end request latency and per-chunk streaming latency. Also export success/error ratio and early-termination counts.
- Auth / quotas: we'll use the redwood_test_key_XXXXX (Logan's stub). I'll update the script to reference the test key placeholder and include a note about header format.

I've attached our annotated script and marked lines with TODOs where FinWise should replace prompt text CSV path. Happy to pair with their infra team tomorrow for a quick run-through.

— Marissa
